newsitem.title: USA: Antibody may slow AIDS -- Sheffield expert.
newsitem.headline: Antibody may slow AIDS -- Sheffield expert.

text.p: Sheffield Medical Technologies Inc said on Wednesday that French researchers whose work it funds published a study linking certain antibodies to higher resistance to AIDS.

Jean-Claude Chermann and two associates wrote an article in AIDS Science indicating that antibodies directed against an epitope of beta-2-microglobulin could be a means of identifying resistance to AIDS.
Sheffield is trying to develop an AIDS vaccine that would induce the production of these antibodies.

It was previously published that these antibodies play some role in inhibiting HIV infections in vitro. Now Chermann and his team said they have found that research subjects who test positive for the disease but develop no symptoms have more of these antibodies than HIV-positive patients who do progress to AIDS.
The article described a way to identify the presence of the antibodies in patient serum.
